title: Mass-imbalanced two-dimensional Bose-Fermi mixtures with boson-fermion pairing
authors: Cristiano Luigi Kosman Chiarappa, Pietro Bovini, Pierbiagio Pieri
abstract: We analyze a two-dimensional Bose-Fermi mixture at zero temperature in the presence of a tunable Bose-Fermi attraction. We adopt a diagrammatic T-matrix approach and study the behavior of several thermodynamic quantities for the two species as functions of density, mass ratio, and coupling strength. These include the chemical potentials, the boson momentum distribution function, the condensate density, and Tan's contact parameter. We analytically demonstrate that the present T-matrix formalism recovers the correct second-order perturbative expansion of the chemical potentials in the weak-coupling regime, and test it numerically. The near-universal behavior already found in prior work for the mass-balanced case is confirmed for different masses and becomes even more accurate when the boson mass is large. The mass imbalance emerges as an additional control parameter that qualitatively affects the bosonic momentum distribution. In particular, we found that it can be used to allow for the experimental observation of a peculiar peak in the boson momentum distribution at finite momentum.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates mass-imbalanced two-dimensional Bose-Fermi mixtures interacting via tunable attraction. Using a diagrammatic T-matrix approach, the authors calculate key thermodynamic properties and predict that mass imbalance introduces qualitative changes in the boson momentum distribution. These findings offer new experimental signatures for probing strongly correlated quantum gases.
main_problem: The study analyzes mass-imbalanced two-dimensional Bose-Fermi (BF) mixtures with tunable boson-fermion attraction at zero temperature.
main_result: Mass imbalance acts as a new control parameter that qualitatively modifies the bosonic momentum distribution, potentially allowing for the observation of a peak at finite momentum.
method: The analysis employs a diagrammatic T-matrix approach and utilizes weak-coupling perturbative expansions to calculate thermodynamic quantities.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a 2D homogeneous mixture of spinless bosons and fermions, governed by an effective Hamiltonian including BF attraction and optional BB repulsion. The study extends theoretical treatments from mass-balanced to mass-imbalanced cases.
key_observables: Chemical potentials ($\mu_B, \mu_F$), boson momentum distribution function ($n_B(k)$), condensate density, and Tan's contact parameter ($C_{BF}$).
important_parameters: Mass ratio ($\gamma_m = m_B/m_F$), boson concentration parameter ($x = n_B/n_F$), and the effective coupling strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a dilute, homogeneous mixture at zero temperature ($T=0$) and relies on diagrammatic approximations (T-matrix formalism).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Feynman diagrams for T-matrices and self-energies; specific plots show the dependence of chemical potentials ($\mu_F, \mu_B$) and the bosonic momentum distribution $n_B(k)$ on mass ratio and coupling strength.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theoretical framework by first establishing the T-matrix formalism in the normal phase, then calculating self-energies for both species, deriving perturbative expansions for chemical potentials ($\mu_F, \mu_B$), and finally analyzing the resulting momentum distributions and condensate fractions as functions of mass imbalance.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced theoretical tools (T-matrix formalism) to predict novel observable signatures (finite momentum peaks) in ultracold quantum gas mixtures, which is highly relevant for experimental realization using modern cold atom or semiconductor platforms.

Full lines correspond to bare bosonic (B) and fermionic (F) Green’s functions, dashed lines correspond to bare BF interactions, and dotted lines with arrows indicate the external momentum flow. (P, Ω) is the center of mass (2+1)-momentum (P, Ω) = (p1+p2, ω1+ω2) while (p, ω) is the exchanged (2+1)-momentum.

FIG. 2. Feynman’s diagrams for the many-body T-matrix in the condensed phase T(P, Ω). Wiggly lines correspond to condensed boson insertions and contribute with a factor of √n0 each, where n0 is the condensate density.
